researchQuestion: How does a non-preemptive priority single-queue multi-server system perform under configurable Poisson arrivals and exponential service times?
scope: Finite discrete-event simulation of one priority queue feeding 1-4 identical servers.
mechanisms: immediate assignment to any idle server
assumptions: Arrivals, priorities, and service durations are independently generated from the fixed seed
Servers are identical and continuously available
A service already in progress is never interrupted
No abandonment, blocking, setup time, or finite capacity
All times are in arbitrary time units
limitations: This is a stochastic teaching model, not calibrated real-world evidence
Finite samples can be noisy and do not establish steady-state performance
Exponential distributions and binary priority may not represent a particular operation
High priority can increase regular-customer waits and starvation is possible
Results depend on the supplied seed and parameters

mean_wait.description: Mean time from arrival until service starts

max_wait.description: Maximum time from arrival until service starts

mean_sojourn.description: Mean time from arrival until service completion
